fun tz id =>
  have times := #[];
  do
  let __s ←
    forIn (*...tz.header.typecnt.toNat) times fun i __s =>
        have times := __s;
        match Std.Time.TimeZone.convertLocalTimeType i tz id with
        | some result =>
          have times := times.push result;
          pure (ForInStep.yield times)
        | x => do
          Except.error
              (toString "cannot convert local time " ++ toString i ++ toString " of the file")
          pure (ForInStep.yield times)
  have times : Array Std.Time.TimeZone.LocalTimeType := __s
  have transitions : Array Std.Time.TimeZone.Transition := #[]
  let __s ←
    forIn (*...tz.transitionTimes.size) transitions fun i __s =>
        have transitions := __s;
        match Std.Time.TimeZone.convertTransition times i tz with
        | some result =>
          have transitions := transitions.push result;
          pure (ForInStep.yield transitions)
        | x => do
          Except.error
              (toString "cannot convert transition " ++ toString i ++ toString " of the file")
          pure (ForInStep.yield transitions)
  have transitions : Array Std.Time.TimeZone.Transition := __s
  have __do_jp : Std.Time.TimeZone.LocalTimeType → Except String Std.Time.TimeZone.ZoneRules :=
    fun initialLocalTimeType =>
    Except.ok { initialLocalTimeType := initialLocalTimeType, transitions := transitions }
  match Std.Time.TimeZone.convertLocalTimeType 0 tz id with
    | some res => do
      let initialLocalTimeType ← Except.ok res
      __do_jp initialLocalTimeType
    | x => do
      let initialLocalTimeType ← Except.error (toString "empty transitions for " ++ toString id)
      __do_jp initialLocalTimeType

fun zonesPaths => do
  let __x ← liftM (IO.getEnv "TZ")
  match __x with
    | some tz =>
      match Std.Time.Database.TZdb.parseTZValue tz with
      | some spec =>
        match spec with
        | Std.Time.Database.TZdb.TZSpec.filePath p =>
          if p.startsWith "/" = true then pure { toString := p }
          else do
            let __do_lift ← Std.Time.Database.TZdb.findInPaths zonesPaths p
            match __do_lift with
              | some path => pure path
              | x =>
                throw
                  (IO.userError
                    (toString "TZ='" ++ toString tz ++ toString "': path '" ++ toString p ++
                      toString "' not found in any zoneinfo directory"))
        | Std.Time.Database.TZdb.TZSpec.zoneId id => do
          let __do_lift ← Std.Time.Database.TZdb.findInPaths zonesPaths id
          match __do_lift with
            | some path => pure path
            | x =>
              throw
                (IO.userError
                  (toString "TZ='" ++ toString tz ++
                    toString "': timezone not found in any zoneinfo directory"))
      | x => pure { toString := "/etc/localtime" }

    fun initialLocalTimeType => do

          if true = true then do

                  have start := res.1;

              | x => pure (ForInStep.done (start, transitions))
          else pure (ForInStep.done (start, transitions))
    have transitions : Array Std.Time.TimeZone.Transition := __s.2
    pure { initialLocalTimeType := initialLocalTimeType, transitions := transitions }
  match __do_lift with
    | some res => do

fun config x =>
  match x with
  | Std.Time.Modifier.G format =>
    match format with
    | Std.Time.Text.short => Std.Time.parseEraShort✝ config.dateformat.symbols
    | Std.Time.Text.full => Std.Time.parseEraLong✝ config.dateformat.symbols
    | Std.Time.Text.narrow => Std.Time.parseEraNarrow✝ config.dateformat.symbols
  | Std.Time.Modifier.y format =>
    match format with
    | Std.Time.Year.any => Int.ofNat <$> Std.Time.parseAtLeastNum✝ 1
    | Std.Time.Year.twoDigit => (fun x => 2000 + x) <$> Int.ofNat <$> Std.Time.parseNum✝ 2
    | Std.Time.Year.fourDigit => Int.ofNat <$> Std.Time.parseNum✝ 4
    | Std.Time.Year.extended n => Int.ofNat <$> Std.Time.parseNum✝ n
  | Std.Time.Modifier.u format =>
    match format with
    | Std.Time.Year.any => Std.Time.parseSigned✝ (Std.Time.parseAtLeastNum✝ 1)
    | Std.Time.Year.twoDigit => (fun x => 2000 + x) <$> Int.ofNat <$> Std.Time.parseNum✝ 2
    | Std.Time.Year.fourDigit => Std.Time.parseSigned✝ (Std.Time.parseNum✝ 4)
    | Std.Time.Year.extended n => Std.Time.parseSigned✝ (Std.Time.parseNum✝ n)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.Y format =>
    match format with
    | Std.Time.Year.any => Std.Time.parseSigned✝ (Std.Time.parseAtLeastNum✝ 1)
    | Std.Time.Year.twoDigit => (fun x => 2000 + x) <$> Int.ofNat <$> Std.Time.parseNum✝ 2
    | Std.Time.Year.fourDigit => Std.Time.parseSigned✝ (Std.Time.parseNum✝ 4)
    | Std.Time.Year.extended n => Std.Time.parseSigned✝ (Std.Time.parseNum✝ n)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.D format =>
    Sigma.mk true <$> Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.MorL format =>
    match format with
    | Sum.inl format => Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding)
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.short => Std.Time.parseMonthShort config.dateformat.symbols
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.full => Std.Time.parseMonthLong✝ config.dateformat.symbols
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.narrow => Std.Time.parseMonthNarrow✝ config.dateformat.symbols
  | Std.Time.Modifier.d format =>
    Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.Qorq format =>
    match format with
    | Sum.inl format => Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding)
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.short => Std.Time.parseQuarterShort✝ config.dateformat.symbols
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.full => Std.Time.parseQuarterLong✝ config.dateformat.symbols
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.narrow => Std.Time.parseQuarterNumber✝
  | Std.Time.Modifier.w format =>
    Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.W format =>
    Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.E format =>
    match format with
    | Std.Time.Text.short => Std.Time.parseWeekdayShort✝ config.dateformat.symbols
    | Std.Time.Text.full => Std.Time.parseWeekdayLong✝ config.dateformat.symbols
    | Std.Time.Text.narrow => Std.Time.parseWeekdayNarrow✝ config.dateformat.symbols
  | Std.Time.Modifier.eorc format =>
    match format with
    | Sum.inl format => do
      let n ← Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding
      have __do_jp :
        Unit →
          Std.Internal.Parsec.String.Parser
            (Std.Time.TypeFormat (Std.Time.Modifier.eorc (Sum.inl format))) :=
        fun __r =>
        have firstOrd := ↑config.dateformat.firstDayOfWeek.toOrdinal;
        have absOrd := (↑n - 1 + firstOrd - 1) % 7 + 1;
        pure
          (Std.Time.Weekday.ofOrdinal
            (Std.Time.Internal.Bounded.LE.ofNatWrapping absOrd Std.Time.parseWith._proof_1✝))
      if ¬(1 ≤ n ∧ n ≤ 7) then do
          let __r ← Std.Internal.Parsec.fail "need a natural number in the interval of 1 to 7"
          __do_jp __r
        else __do_jp ()
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.short => Std.Time.parseWeekdayShort✝ config.dateformat.symbols
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.full => Std.Time.parseWeekdayLong✝ config.dateformat.symbols
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.narrow => Std.Time.parseWeekdayNarrow✝ config.dateformat.symbols
  | Std.Time.Modifier.F format =>
    Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.a format =>
    match format with
    | Std.Time.Text.short => Std.Time.parseMarkerShort✝ config.dateformat.symbols
    | Std.Time.Text.full => Std.Time.parseMarkerLong✝ config.dateformat.symbols
    | Std.Time.Text.narrow => Std.Time.parseMarkerNarrow✝ config.dateformat.symbols
  | Std.Time.Modifier.h format =>
    Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.K format =>
    Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.k format =>
    Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.H format =>
    Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.m format =>
    Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.s format =>
    if config.allowLeapSeconds = true then
      Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding)
    else do
      let res ← Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding)
      pure (res.expandTop Std.Time.parseWith._proof_2✝)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.S format =>
    match format with
    | Std.Time.Fraction.nano => Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ 9)
    | Std.Time.Fraction.truncated n => Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFractionNum✝ n 9)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.A format =>
    Std.Time.Millisecond.Offset.ofNat <$> Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding
  | Std.Time.Modifier.n format =>
    Std.Time.parseNatToBounded✝ (Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.N format =>
    Std.Time.Nanosecond.Offset.ofNat <$> Std.Time.parseFlexibleNum✝ format.padding
  | Std.Time.Modifier.V => Std.Time.parseIdentifier✝
  | Std.Time.Modifier.z format =>
    match format with
    | Std.Time.ZoneName.short => Std.Time.parseIdentifier✝
    | Std.Time.ZoneName.full => Std.Time.parseIdentifier✝
  | Std.Time.Modifier.O format =>
    match format with
    | Std.Time.OffsetO.short =>
      Std.Internal.Parsec.String.pstring "GMT" *>
        Std.Time.parseOffset✝ Std.Time.Reason.no✝ Std.Time.Reason.no✝ false
    | Std.Time.OffsetO.full =>
      Std.Internal.Parsec.String.pstring "GMT" *>
        Std.Time.parseOffset✝ Std.Time.Reason.yes✝ Std.Time.Reason.optional✝ false
  | Std.Time.Modifier.X format =>
    have p :=
      match format with
      | Std.Time.OffsetX.hour => Std.Time.parseOffset✝ Std.Time.Reason.no✝ Std.Time.Reason.no✝ false
      | Std.Time.OffsetX.hourMinute =>
        Std.Time.parseOffset✝ Std.Time.Reason.yes✝ Std.Time.Reason.no✝ false
      | Std.Time.OffsetX.hourMinuteColon =>
        Std.Time.parseOffset✝ Std.Time.Reason.yes✝ Std.Time.Reason.no✝ true
      | Std.Time.OffsetX.hourMinuteSecond =>
        Std.Time.parseOffset✝ Std.Time.Reason.yes✝ Std.Time.Reason.yes✝ false
      | Std.Time.OffsetX.hourMinuteSecondColon =>
        Std.Time.parseOffset✝ Std.Time.Reason.yes✝ Std.Time.Reason.yes✝ true;
    p <|> Std.Internal.Parsec.String.pstring "Z" *> pure { second := 0 }
  | Std.Time.Modifier.x format =>
    match format with
    | Std.Time.OffsetX.hour =>
      Std.Time.parseOffset✝ Std.Time.Reason.optional✝ Std.Time.Reason.no✝ false
    | Std.Time.OffsetX.hourMinute =>
      Std.Time.parseOffset✝ Std.Time.Reason.yes✝ Std.Time.Reason.no✝ false
    | Std.Time.OffsetX.hourMinuteColon =>
      Std.Time.parseOffset✝ Std.Time.Reason.yes✝ Std.Time.Reason.optional✝ true
    | Std.Time.OffsetX.hourMinuteSecond =>
      Std.Time.parseOffset✝ Std.Time.Reason.yes✝ Std.Time.Reason.optional✝ false
    | Std.Time.OffsetX.hourMinuteSecondColon =>
      Std.Time.parseOffset✝ Std.Time.Reason.yes✝ Std.Time.Reason.yes✝ true
  | Std.Time.Modifier.Z format =>
    match format with
    | Std.Time.OffsetZ.hourMinute =>
      Std.Time.parseOffset✝ Std.Time.Reason.yes✝ Std.Time.Reason.no✝ false
    | Std.Time.OffsetZ.full => do
      Std.Internal.Parsec.String.skipString "GMT"
      let res ← optional (Std.Time.parseOffset✝ Std.Time.Reason.yes✝ Std.Time.Reason.no✝ true)
      pure (res.getD Std.Time.TimeZone.Offset.zero)
    | Std.Time.OffsetZ.hourMinuteSecondColon =>
      Std.Internal.Parsec.String.skipString "Z" *> pure Std.Time.TimeZone.Offset.zero <|>
        Std.Time.parseOffset✝ Std.Time.Reason.yes✝ Std.Time.Reason.optional✝ true

fun dateformat modifier data =>
  match modifier, data with
  | Std.Time.Modifier.G format, data =>
    match format, data with
    | Std.Time.Text.short, data => Std.Time.formatEraShort✝ dateformat.symbols data
    | Std.Time.Text.full, data => Std.Time.formatEraLong✝ dateformat.symbols data
    | Std.Time.Text.narrow, data => Std.Time.formatEraNarrow✝ dateformat.symbols data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.y format, data =>
    have info := Std.Time.Year.Offset.toInt data;
    have info := if info ≤ 0 then -info + 1 else info;
    match format, data with
    | Std.Time.Year.any, data => Std.Time.pad✝ 0 info
    | Std.Time.Year.twoDigit, data => Std.Time.pad✝ 2 (info % 100)
    | Std.Time.Year.fourDigit, data => Std.Time.pad✝ 4 info
    | Std.Time.Year.extended n, data => Std.Time.pad✝ n info
  | Std.Time.Modifier.u format, data =>
    match format, data with
    | Std.Time.Year.any, data => Std.Time.pad✝ 0 (Std.Time.Year.Offset.toInt data)
    | Std.Time.Year.twoDigit, data => Std.Time.pad✝ 2 (Std.Time.Year.Offset.toInt data % 100)
    | Std.Time.Year.fourDigit, data => Std.Time.pad✝ 4 (Std.Time.Year.Offset.toInt data)
    | Std.Time.Year.extended n, data => Std.Time.pad✝ n (Std.Time.Year.Offset.toInt data)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.Y format, data =>
    have info := Std.Time.Year.Offset.toInt data;
    have info := if info ≤ 0 then -info + 1 else info;
    match format, data with
    | Std.Time.Year.any, data => Std.Time.pad✝ 0 info
    | Std.Time.Year.twoDigit, data => Std.Time.pad✝ 2 (info % 100)
    | Std.Time.Year.fourDigit, data => Std.Time.pad✝ 4 info
    | Std.Time.Year.extended n, data => Std.Time.pad✝ n info
  | Std.Time.Modifier.D format, data => Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding ↑data.snd
  | Std.Time.Modifier.MorL format, data =>
    match format, data with
    | Sum.inl format, data => Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding ↑data
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.short, data => Std.Time.formatMonthShort✝ dateformat.symbols data
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.full, data => Std.Time.formatMonthLong✝ dateformat.symbols data
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.narrow, data => Std.Time.formatMonthNarrow✝ dateformat.symbols data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.d format, data => Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding ↑data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.Qorq format, data =>
    match format, data with
    | Sum.inl format, data => Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding ↑data
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.short, data => Std.Time.formatQuarterShort✝ dateformat.symbols data
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.full, data => Std.Time.formatQuarterLong✝ dateformat.symbols data
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.narrow, data => Std.Time.formatQuarterNumber✝ data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.w format, data => Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding ↑data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.W format, data => Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding ↑data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.E format, data =>
    match format, data with
    | Std.Time.Text.short, data => Std.Time.formatWeekdayShort✝ dateformat.symbols data
    | Std.Time.Text.full, data => Std.Time.formatWeekdayLong✝ dateformat.symbols data
    | Std.Time.Text.narrow, data => Std.Time.formatWeekdayNarrow✝ dateformat.symbols data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.eorc format, data =>
    match format, data with
    | Sum.inl format, data =>
      have firstOrd := ↑dateformat.firstDayOfWeek.toOrdinal;
      have dayOrd := ↑(Std.Time.Weekday.toOrdinal data);
      Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding ((dayOrd - firstOrd + 7) % 7 + 1)
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.short, data => Std.Time.formatWeekdayShort✝ dateformat.symbols data
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.full, data => Std.Time.formatWeekdayLong✝ dateformat.symbols data
    | Sum.inr Std.Time.Text.narrow, data => Std.Time.formatWeekdayNarrow✝ dateformat.symbols data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.F format, data => Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding ↑data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.a format, data =>
    match format, data with
    | Std.Time.Text.short, data => Std.Time.formatMarkerShort✝ dateformat.symbols data
    | Std.Time.Text.full, data => Std.Time.formatMarkerLong✝ dateformat.symbols data
    | Std.Time.Text.narrow, data => Std.Time.formatMarkerNarrow✝ dateformat.symbols data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.h format, data => Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding (↑data % 12)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.K format, data => Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding (↑data % 12)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.k format, data => Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding ↑data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.H format, data => Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding ↑data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.m format, data => Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding ↑data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.s format, data => Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding ↑data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.S format, data =>
    match format, data with
    | Std.Time.Fraction.nano, data => Std.Time.pad✝ 9 ↑data
    | Std.Time.Fraction.truncated n, data => Std.Time.rightTruncate✝ n (↑data) true
  | Std.Time.Modifier.A format, data => Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding data.val
  | Std.Time.Modifier.n format, data => Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding ↑data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.N format, data => Std.Time.pad✝ format.padding data.val
  | Std.Time.Modifier.V, data => data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.z format, data =>
    match format, data with
    | Std.Time.ZoneName.short, data => data
    | Std.Time.ZoneName.full, data => data
  | Std.Time.Modifier.O format, data =>
    match format, data with
    | Std.Time.OffsetO.short, data =>
      toString "GMT" ++
        toString (Std.Time.toSigned✝ (Std.Time.Internal.UnitVal.toInt data.second.toHours))
    | Std.Time.OffsetO.full, data =>
      toString "GMT" ++ toString (Std.Time.toIsoString✝ data true false true)
  | Std.Time.Modifier.X format, data =>
    if (data.second == 0) = true then "Z"
    else
      match format, data with
      | Std.Time.OffsetX.hour, data => Std.Time.toIsoString✝ data false false false
      | Std.Time.OffsetX.hourMinute, data => Std.Time.toIsoString✝ data true false false
      | Std.Time.OffsetX.hourMinuteColon, data => Std.Time.toIsoString✝ data true false true
      | Std.Time.OffsetX.hourMinuteSecond, data => Std.Time.toIsoString✝ data true true false
      | Std.Time.OffsetX.hourMinuteSecondColon, data => Std.Time.toIsoString✝ data true true true
  | Std.Time.Modifier.x format, data =>
    match format, data with
    | Std.Time.OffsetX.hour, data =>
      Std.Time.toIsoString✝ data (decide (data.second.toMinutes.val % 60 ≠ 0)) false false
    | Std.Time.OffsetX.hourMinute, data => Std.Time.toIsoString✝ data true false false
    | Std.Time.OffsetX.hourMinuteColon, data =>
      Std.Time.toIsoString✝ data true (decide (data.second.val % 60 ≠ 0)) true
    | Std.Time.OffsetX.hourMinuteSecond, data =>
      Std.Time.toIsoString✝ data true (decide (data.second.val % 60 ≠ 0)) false
    | Std.Time.OffsetX.hourMinuteSecondColon, data => Std.Time.toIsoString✝ data true true true
  | Std.Time.Modifier.Z format, data =>
    match format, data with
    | Std.Time.OffsetZ.hourMinute, data => Std.Time.toIsoString✝ data true false false
    | Std.Time.OffsetZ.full, data =>
      if data.second.val = 0 then "GMT"
      else toString "GMT" ++ toString (Std.Time.toIsoString✝ data true false true)
    | Std.Time.OffsetZ.hourMinuteSecondColon, data =>
      if (data.second == 0) = true then "Z"
      else Std.Time.toIsoString✝ data true (decide (data.second.val % 60 ≠ 0)) true

fun withMinutes withSeconds withColon => do
  let sign ←
    Std.Internal.Parsec.String.pchar '+' *> pure 1 <|>
        Std.Internal.Parsec.String.pchar '-' *> pure (-1)
  let hours ←
    Std.Time.Internal.UnitVal.ofInt <$> do
        let a ← Std.Time.parseNum✝ 2
        pure ↑a
  have __do_jp : Unit → Std.Internal.Parsec.String.Parser Std.Time.TimeZone.Offset := fun __r =>
    have colon := if withColon = true then Std.Internal.Parsec.String.pchar ':' else pure ':';
    have parseUnit := fun {n} reason =>
      match reason with
      | Std.Time.Reason.yes✝ =>
        some <$>
          (colon *>
            Std.Time.Internal.UnitVal.ofInt <$> do
              let a ← Std.Time.parseNum✝ 2
              pure ↑a)
      | Std.Time.Reason.no✝ => pure none
      | Std.Time.Reason.optional✝ =>
        optional
          (colon *>
            Std.Time.Internal.UnitVal.ofInt <$> do
              let a ← Std.Time.parseNum✝ 2
              pure ↑a);
    do
    let minutes ← parseUnit withMinutes
    have __do_jp : Unit → Std.Internal.Parsec.String.Parser Std.Time.TimeZone.Offset := fun __r =>
      do
      let seconds ← parseUnit withSeconds
      have __do_jp : Unit → Std.Internal.Parsec.String.Parser Std.Time.TimeZone.Offset := fun __r =>
        have hours := hours.toSeconds + (minutes.getD 0).toSeconds + seconds.getD 0;
        pure { second := { val := hours.val * sign } }
      match seconds with
        | some s =>
          if s.val > 59 then do
            let __r ←
              Std.Internal.Parsec.fail
                  (toString "invalid second offset: " ++ toString s.val ++
                    toString ". Must be between 0 and 59.")
            __do_jp __r
          else __do_jp ()
        | x => __do_jp ()
    match minutes with
      | some m =>
        if m.val > 59 then do
          let __r ←
            Std.Internal.Parsec.fail
                (toString "invalid minute offset: " ++ toString m.val ++
                  toString ". Must be between 0 and 59.")
          __do_jp __r
        else __do_jp ()
      | x => __do_jp ()
  if hours.val < 0 ∨ hours.val > 23 then do
      let __r ←
        Std.Internal.Parsec.fail
            (toString "invalid hour offset: " ++ toString hours.val ++
              toString ". Must be between 0 and 23.")
      __do_jp __r
    else __do_jp ()

  | Except.ok res => do
    let alts ← List.mapM Std.Time.convertFormatPart✝ res.string
    have alts : Lean.Syntax.TSepArray `term "," :=
      List.foldl Lean.Syntax.TSepArray.push { elemsAndSeps := #[] } alts

fun date format locale =>
  have format := Std.Time.GenericFormat.spec format;
  match format with
  | Except.error err => toString "error: " ++ toString err
  | Except.ok res =>
    have res :=
      res.formatGeneric fun x =>
        match x with
        | Std.Time.Modifier.G presentation => some date.era
        | Std.Time.Modifier.y presentation => some date.year
        | Std.Time.Modifier.u presentation => some date.year
        | Std.Time.Modifier.Y presentation => some (date.weekYear locale.firstDayOfWeek)
        | Std.Time.Modifier.D presentation => some ⟨date.year.isLeap, date.dayOfYear⟩
        | Std.Time.Modifier.Qorq presentation => some date.quarter
        | Std.Time.Modifier.w presentation => some (date.weekOfYear locale.firstDayOfWeek)
        | Std.Time.Modifier.W presentation => some (date.alignedWeekOfMonth locale.firstDayOfWeek)
        | Std.Time.Modifier.MorL presentation => some date.month
        | Std.Time.Modifier.d presentation => some date.day
        | Std.Time.Modifier.E presentation => some date.weekday
        | Std.Time.Modifier.eorc presentation => some date.weekday
        | Std.Time.Modifier.F presentation => some date.weekOfMonth
        | x => none;
    match res with
    | some res => res
    | none => "invalid time"

value.text:
fun date format locale =>
  have format := Std.Time.GenericFormat.spec format;
  match format with
  | Except.error err => toString "error: " ++ toString err
  | Except.ok res =>
    have res :=
      res.formatGeneric fun x =>
        match x with
        | Std.Time.Modifier.G presentation => some date.era
        | Std.Time.Modifier.y presentation => some date.year
        | Std.Time.Modifier.u presentation => some date.year
        | Std.Time.Modifier.Y presentation => some (date.weekYear locale.firstDayOfWeek)
        | Std.Time.Modifier.D presentation => some ⟨date.year.isLeap, date.dayOfYear⟩
        | Std.Time.Modifier.Qorq presentation => some date.quarter
        | Std.Time.Modifier.w presentation => some (date.weekOfYear locale.firstDayOfWeek)
        | Std.Time.Modifier.W presentation => some (date.alignedWeekOfMonth locale.firstDayOfWeek)
        | Std.Time.Modifier.MorL presentation => some date.month
        | Std.Time.Modifier.d presentation => some date.day
        | Std.Time.Modifier.E presentation => some date.weekday
        | Std.Time.Modifier.eorc presentation => some date.weekday
        | Std.Time.Modifier.F presentation => some date.weekOfMonth
        | Std.Time.Modifier.H presentation => some date.hour

doc: Combine two premise selectors, returning the best suggestions.

value.text:
fun selector₁ selector₂ g c => do
  let suggestions₁ ← selector₁ g c
  let suggestions₂ ← selector₂ g c
  have dedupMap : Std.HashMap (Lean.Name × Option String) Lean.LibrarySuggestions.Suggestion := ∅
  let __s ←
    forIn (suggestions₁ ++ suggestions₂) dedupMap fun s __s =>
        have dedupMap := __s;
        have key := (s.name, s.flag);
        have dedupMap :=
          dedupMap.alter key fun x =>
            match x with
            | none => some s
            | some s' => if s.score > s'.score then some s else some s';
        pure (ForInStep.yield dedupMap)
  have dedupMap : Std.HashMap (Lean.Name × Option String) Lean.LibrarySuggestions.Suggestion := __s
  have deduped : Array Lean.LibrarySuggestions.Suggestion := dedupMap.valuesArray
  have sorted : Array Lean.LibrarySuggestions.Suggestion :=
    deduped.qsort fun s₁ s₂ => decide (s₁.score > s₂.score)
  pure (sorted.take c.maxSuggestions)

doc:
`#check_assertions` retrieves all declarations and all imports that were declared
not to exist so far (including in transitively imported files) and reports their current
status:
* ✓ means the declaration or import exists,
* × means the declaration or import does not exist.

This means that the expectation is that all checks *succeed* by the time `#check_assertions`
is used, typically once all of the library has been built.

If all declarations and imports are available when `#check_assertions` is used,
then the command logs an info message. Otherwise, it emits a warning.

The variant `#check_assertions!` only prints declarations/imports that are not present in the
environment. In particular, it is silent if everything is imported, making it useful for testing.

fun stx =>
  have tk := stx[1];
  do
  let env ← Lean.getEnv
  have entries : Array Lean.Elab.Command.AssertExists := Lean.Elab.Command.getSortedAssertExists env
  if (entries.isEmpty && tk.isNone) = true then
      Lean.logInfo ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) "No assertions made.")
    else
      have allMods := env.allImportedModuleNames;
      have msgs := #[Lean.toMessageData ""];
      have outcome := Lean.toMessageData "";
      have allExist? := true;
      do
      let __s ←
        forIn entries (msgs, outcome, allExist?) fun d __s =>
            have msgs := __s.1;
            have __s := __s.2;
            have allExist? := __s.2;
            have type := if d.isDecl = true then "declaration" else "module";
            have cond :=
              if d.isDecl = true then env.contains d.givenName else allMods.contains d.givenName;
            have outcome :=
              if cond = true then Lean.toMessageData Lean.checkEmoji
              else Lean.toMessageData Lean.crossEmoji;
            have allExist? := allExist? && cond;
            if (tk.isNone || !cond) = true then
              have msgs :=
                msgs.push
                  (Lean.toMessageData outcome ++ Lean.toMessageData " '" ++
                              Lean.toMessageData d.givenName ++
                            Lean.toMessageData "' (" ++
                          Lean.toMessageData type ++
                        Lean.toMessageData ") asserted in '" ++
                      Lean.toMessageData d.modName ++
                    Lean.toMessageData "'.");
              pure (ForInStep.yield (msgs, outcome, allExist?))
            else pure (ForInStep.yield (msgs, outcome, allExist?))
      have msgs : Array Lean.MessageData := __s.1
      have __s : Lean.MessageData × Bool := __s.2
      have allExist? : Bool := __s.2
      have msgs : Array Lean.MessageData :=
        ((msgs.push (Lean.toMessageData "---")).push
              (Lean.toMessageData Lean.checkEmoji ++
                Lean.toMessageData " means the declaration or import exists.")).push
          (Lean.toMessageData Lean.crossEmoji ++
            Lean.toMessageData " means the declaration or import does not exist.")
      have msg : Lean.MessageData :=
        Lean.MessageData.joinSep msgs.toList ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format) "\n")
      have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.Elab.Command.CommandElabM Unit := fun __r =>
        if (!allExist?) = true then Lean.logWarning msg else pure ()
      if (allExist? && tk.isNone) = true then do
          let __r ← Lean.logInfo msg
          __do_jp __r
        else __do_jp ()

doc:
`assert_not_exists d₁ d₂ ... dₙ` is a command that asserts that the declarations named
`d₁ d₂ ... dₙ` *do not exist* in the current import scope.

Be careful to use names (e.g. `Rat`) rather than notations (e.g. `ℚ`).

It may be used (sparingly!) to enforce plans that certain files are independent of each other.

If you encounter an error on an `assert_not_exists` command while developing a library,
it is probably because you have introduced new import dependencies to a file.
In this case, you should refactor your work
(for example by creating new files rather than adding imports to existing files).
You should *not* delete the `assert_not_exists` statement without careful discussion ahead of time.

`assert_not_exists` statements should generally live at the top of the file, after the module doc.

fun stx => do
  let env ← Lean.getEnv
  forIn stx[1].getArgs PUnit.unit fun n __s => do
      let e ←
        tryCatch
            (do
              let decl ←
                Lean.Elab.Command.liftCoreM (Lean.Elab.realizeGlobalConstNoOverloadWithInfo n)
              OptionT.run (pure decl))
            fun x => do
            let __do_lift ← Lean.getMainModule
            Lean.Elab.Command.addAssertExistsEntry true n.getId __do_lift
            ContinueT.continue
      Continue.runK e (fun r => pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)) fun decl => do
          let c ← Lean.mkConstWithLevelParams decl
          let msg ←
            match env.getModuleIdxFor? decl with
              | some idx =>
                have idx := idx;
                pure
                  (Lean.toMessageData "Declaration " ++ Lean.toMessageData c ++
                      Lean.toMessageData
                        " is not allowed to be imported by this file.\nIt is defined in " ++
                    Lean.toMessageData (Lean.Elab.Command.importPathMessage env idx))
              | x =>
                pure
                  (Lean.toMessageData "Declaration " ++ Lean.toMessageData c ++
                    Lean.toMessageData " is defined in this file.")
          Lean.logErrorAt n
              (Lean.toMessageData msg ++
                Lean.toMessageData
                  "\n\nThese invariants are maintained by `assert_not_exists` statements, and exist in order to ensure that \"complicated\" parts of the library are not accidentally introduced as dependencies of \"simple\" parts of the library.")
          pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
  pure ()

fun x x_1 =>

The `directoryDependency` linter detects imports between directories that are supposed to be
independent. If this is the case, it emits a warning.

value.text:
fun mainModule => do
  let __do_lift ← Lean.Linter.getLinterOptions
  if Lean.Linter.getLinterValue Mathlib.Linter.linter.directoryDependency __do_lift = true then do
      let env ← Lean.getEnv
      have imports : Array Lean.Name := env.allImportedModuleNames
      have matchingPrefixes : Lean.NameSet :=
        Lean.NameSet.filter
          (fun prf =>
            Mathlib.Linter.DirectoryDependency.NamePrefixRel.containsKey✝
              Mathlib.Linter.DirectoryDependency.allowedImportDirs✝ prf)
          (Lean.Name.prefixes✝ mainModule)
      if Std.TreeSet.isEmpty matchingPrefixes = true then
          match Mathlib.Linter.checkBlocklist✝ env mainModule imports with
          | some msg => pure #[msg]
          | x => pure #[]
        else do
          let __do_lift ←
            liftM (findImports ({ toString := "Mathlib" } / { toString := "Init.lean" }))
          have initImports : Array Lean.Name :=
            __do_lift.append #[`Mathlib.Init, `Mathlib.Tactic.DeclarationNames]
          have exclude : List Lean.Name :=
            [`Init, `Std, `Lean, `Aesop, `Qq, `Plausible, `ImportGraph, `ProofWidgets,
              `LeanSearchClient]
          have importsToCheck : Array Lean.Name :=
            Array.filter (fun x => !initImports.contains x)
              (Array.filter (fun imp => !Std.TreeSet.any matchingPrefixes fun x => x.isPrefixOf imp)
                (Array.filter (fun imp => !exclude.any fun x => x.isPrefixOf imp) imports))
          have allRules : Lean.NameSet :=
            Mathlib.Linter.DirectoryDependency.NamePrefixRel.getAllLeft✝
              Mathlib.Linter.DirectoryDependency.allowedImportDirs✝ mainModule
          have messages : Array Lean.MessageData := #[]
          let __s ←
            forIn importsToCheck messages fun imported __s =>
                have messages := __s;
                if
                    (!Mathlib.Linter.DirectoryDependency.NamePrefixRel.contains✝
                          Mathlib.Linter.DirectoryDependency.allowedImportDirs✝ mainModule
                          imported) =
                      true then
                  have importPath := env.importPath imported;
                  have msg :=
                    Lean.toMessageData "Module " ++ Lean.toMessageData mainModule ++
                                Lean.toMessageData " depends on " ++
                              Lean.toMessageData imported ++
                            Lean.toMessageData
                              ",\nbut is only allowed to import modules starting with one of " ++
                          Lean.toMessageData
                            ((Std.TreeSet.toArray allRules).qsort fun x1 x2 =>
                              decide (x1.toString < x2.toString)) ++
                        Lean.toMessageData ".\nNote: module " ++
                      Lean.toMessageData imported;
                  have superseded := false;
                  have __do_jp := fun __r msg superseded =>
                    if (!superseded) = true then
                      have messages := messages.push msg;
                      pure (ForInStep.yield messages)
                    else pure (ForInStep.yield messages);
                  match importPath.toList with
                  | [] =>
                    have msg :=
                      msg ++
                        (Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
                          " is directly imported by this module";
                    __do_jp () msg superseded
                  | a :: rest =>
                    if
                        (!Mathlib.Linter.DirectoryDependency.NamePrefixRel.contains✝
                              Mathlib.Linter.DirectoryDependency.allowedImportDirs✝ mainModule a) =
                          true then
                      have superseded := true;
                      __do_jp () msg superseded
                    else
                      have msg :=
                        msg ++
                          (Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
                            (toString " is imported by " ++ toString a ++ toString ",\n");
                      do
                      let __s ←
                        forIn rest (msg, superseded) fun dep __s =>
                            have msg := __s.1;
                            have superseded := __s.2;
                            if
                                (!Mathlib.Linter.DirectoryDependency.NamePrefixRel.contains✝
                                      Mathlib.Linter.DirectoryDependency.allowedImportDirs✝
                                      mainModule dep) =
                                  true then
                              have superseded := true;
                              pure (ForInStep.done (msg, superseded))
                            else
                              have msg :=
                                msg ++
                                  (Lean.toMessageData "which is imported by " ++
                                      Lean.toMessageData dep ++
                                    Lean.toMessageData ",\n");
                              pure (ForInStep.yield (msg, superseded))
                      have msg : Lean.MessageData := __s.1
                      have superseded : Bool := __s.2
                      have msg : Lean.MessageData :=
                        msg ++ Lean.toMessageData "which is imported by this module."
                      have msg : Lean.MessageData :=
                        msg ++
                          (Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
                            "(Exceptions can be added to `allowedImportDirs`.)"
                      __do_jp () msg superseded
                else pure (ForInStep.yield messages)
          have messages : Array Lean.MessageData := __s
          pure messages
    else pure #[]

fun env mainModule imports =>
  (match
      Mathlib.Linter.DirectoryDependency.NamePrefixRel.findAny✝
        Mathlib.Linter.DirectoryDependency.forbiddenImportDirs✝ mainModule imports with
    | some (n₁, n₂) =>
      match Lean.Name.prefixToName✝ n₂ imports with
      | some imported =>
        if
            (!Mathlib.Linter.DirectoryDependency.NamePrefixRel.contains✝
                  Mathlib.Linter.DirectoryDependency.overrideAllowedImportDirs✝ mainModule
                  imported) =
              true then
          have msg :=
            Lean.toMessageData "Modules starting with " ++ Lean.toMessageData n₁ ++
                      Lean.toMessageData " are not allowed to import modules starting with " ++
                    Lean.toMessageData n₂ ++
                  Lean.toMessageData ". This module depends on " ++
                Lean.toMessageData imported ++
              Lean.toMessageData "\n";
          do
          let __s ←
            forIn (env.importPath imported) msg fun dep __s =>
                have msg := __s;
                have msg :=
                  msg ++
                    (Lean.toMessageData "which is imported by " ++ Lean.toMessageData dep ++
                      Lean.toMessageData ",\n");
                pure (ForInStep.yield msg)
          have msg : Lean.MessageData := __s
          pure
              (some
                (msg ++
                  Lean.toMessageData
                    "which is imported by this module. (Exceptions can be added to `overrideAllowedImportDirs`.)"))
        else none
      | x =>
        pure
          (some
            (Lean.toMessageData
                  "Internal error in `directoryDependency` linter: this module claims to depend on a module starting with " ++
                Lean.toMessageData n₂ ++
              Lean.toMessageData
                " but a module with that prefix was not found in the import graph."))
    | none => none).run

doc:
`parseUpToHere pos post` takes as input `pos : String.Pos` and the optional `post : String`.
It parses the current file from the beginning until `pos`, appending `post` at the end.
It returns a syntax node of kind `Lean.Parser.Module.module`.
The option of appending a final string to the text gives more control to avoid syntax errors,
for instance in the presence of `#guard_msgs in` or `set_option ... in`.

Note that this parsing will *not* be successful on every file.  However, if the linter is
parsing the file linearly, it will only need to parse
* the imports (that are always parseable) and
* the first non-import command that is supposed to be a module doc-string (so again always
  parseable).

In conclusion, either the parsing is successful, and the linter can continue with its analysis,
or the parsing is not successful and the linter will flag a missing module doc-string!

  Lean.Elab.Command.CommandElabM Lean.Syntax

fun pos post => do
  let __do_lift ← Lean.getFileMap
  have upToHere : Substring.Raw := { str := __do_lift.source, startPos := { }, stopPos := pos }
  let __do_lift ← Lean.getEnv
  liftM (Lean.Parser.testParseModule __do_lift "linter.style.header" (upToHere.toString ++ post))

fun importStx => do
  guard (importStx.isOfKind `Lean.Parser.Module.import = true)
  have args : Array Lean.Syntax := importStx.getArgs
  let moduleId ← (Array.filter (fun x => x.isIdent) args).back?
  have allAtoms : Array String := Mathlib.Linter.Style.header.collectAtoms✝ importStx
  have isPublic : Bool := allAtoms.contains "public"
  have isMeta : Bool := allAtoms.contains "meta"
  have isAll : Bool := allAtoms.contains "all"
  pure (moduleId, isPublic, isMeta, isAll)

fun imports mainModule => do
  forIn imports PUnit.unit fun i __s =>
      match i.getId with
      | `Mathlib.Tactic => do
        Lean.Linter.logLint Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.header i
            ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
              (toString "Files in mathlib cannot import the whole `" ++ toString i.getId ++
                toString "` folder. Doing so would cause imports to be unnecessarily slow."))
        pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
      | `Lean => do
        Lean.Linter.logLint Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.header i
            ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
              (toString "Files in mathlib cannot import the whole `" ++ toString i.getId ++
                toString "` folder. Doing so would cause imports to be unnecessarily slow."))
        pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
      | `Lean.Meta => do
        Lean.Linter.logLint Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.header i
            ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
              (toString "Files in mathlib cannot import the whole `" ++ toString i.getId ++
                toString "` folder. Doing so would cause imports to be unnecessarily slow."))
        pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
      | `Lean.Elab => do
        Lean.Linter.logLint Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.header i
            ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
              (toString "Files in mathlib cannot import the whole `" ++ toString i.getId ++
                toString "` folder. Doing so would cause imports to be unnecessarily slow."))
        pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
      | `Lean.Elab.Tactic => do
        Lean.Linter.logLint Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.header i
            ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
              (toString "Files in mathlib cannot import the whole `" ++ toString i.getId ++
                toString "` folder. Doing so would cause imports to be unnecessarily slow."))
        pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
      | `Std => do
        Lean.Linter.logLint Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.header i
            ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
              (toString "Files in mathlib cannot import the whole `" ++ toString i.getId ++
                toString "` folder. Doing so would cause imports to be unnecessarily slow."))
        pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
      | `Mathlib.Tactic.Replace =>
        if (mainModule != `Mathlib.Tactic) = true then do
          Lean.Linter.logLint Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.header i
              ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
                "'Mathlib.Tactic.Replace' defines a deprecated form of the 'replace' tactic; please do not use it in mathlib.")
          pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
        else pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
      | `Mathlib.Tactic.Have =>
        if (! [`Mathlib.Tactic, `Mathlib.Tactic.Replace].contains mainModule) = true then do
          Lean.Linter.logLint Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.header i
              ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
                "'Mathlib.Tactic.Have' defines a deprecated form of the 'have' tactic; please do not use it in mathlib.")
          pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
        else pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
      | modName =>
        if (modName.getRoot == `Lake) = true then do
          Lean.Linter.logLint Mathlib.Linter.linter.style.header i
              ((Lean.MessageData.ofFormat ∘ Std.format)
                "In the past, importing 'Lake' in mathlib has led to dramatic slow-downs of the linter (see e.g. https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/pull/13779). Please consider carefully if this import is useful and make sure to benchmark it. If this is fine, feel free to silence this linter.")
          pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
        else pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
  pure ()

Return if `line` looks like a correct authors line in a copyright header.

The `offset` input is used to shift the position information of the `Syntax` that the command
produces.
`authorsLineChecks` computes a position for its warning *relative to `line`*.
The `offset` input passes on the starting position of `line` in the whole file.

  Array (Lean.Syntax × String)

value.text:
fun line offset =>
  (have stxs := #[];
    have __do_jp := fun __r stxs =>
      have __do_jp := fun __r stxs =>
        have __do_jp := fun __r stxs =>
          have __do_jp := fun __r stxs =>
            if (!stxs.isEmpty) = true then pure stxs
            else
              if (line.drop "Authors:".length).trimAscii.isEmpty = true then
                pure
                  #[(Mathlib.Linter.toSyntax✝ line "Authors:" offset,
                      toString "Please, add at least one author!")]
              else pure #[];
          if (line.back == '.') = true then
            have stxs :=
              stxs.push
                (Mathlib.Linter.toSyntax✝ line "." offset,
                  toString "Please, do not end the authors' line with a period.");
            __do_jp () stxs
          else __do_jp () stxs;
        if ((line.splitOn " and ").length != 1) = true then
          have stxs :=
            stxs.push
              (Mathlib.Linter.toSyntax✝ line " and " offset,
                toString "Please, do not use 'and'; use ',' instead.");
          __do_jp () stxs
        else __do_jp () stxs;
      if ((line.splitOn "  ").length != 1) = true then
        have stxs :=
          stxs.push
            (Mathlib.Linter.toSyntax✝ line "  " offset, toString "Double spaces are not allowed.");
        __do_jp () stxs
      else __do_jp () stxs;
    if (!line.startsWith "Authors: ") = true then
      have stxs :=
        stxs.push
          (Mathlib.Linter.toSyntax✝ line (line.take "Authors: ".length).copy offset,
            toString "The authors line should begin with 'Authors: '");
      __do_jp () stxs
    else __do_jp () stxs).run

`isInLibraryRoot modName` returns `true` if `<root>.lean` imports the file `modName`, where
`<root>` is the top-level component of `modName`. For example, for `Mathlib.Foo.Bar` this checks
`Mathlib.lean`; for `Cslib.Foo.Bar` this checks `Cslib.lean`.

so that the linter works in any project whose library root follows the standard Lean convention
of being named after the top-level module.

  let __do_lift ← ST.Ref.get Lean.Server.builtinRpcProcedures✝
  match Lean.PersistentHashMap.find? __do_lift p.method with
    | some proc =>
      (do

          let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Server.ServerTask.wait t)
          match __do_lift with
            | Except.ok r => pure r
            | Except.error err => throw err).asTask
    | x => do
      let doc ← Lean.Server.RequestM.readDoc
      have text : Lean.FileMap := doc.meta.text
      have callPos : String.Pos.Raw := text.lspPosToUtf8Pos p.position
      have throwNotFound : Lean.Server.RequestM (Lean.Server.RequestTask Lean.Json) :=
        throwThe Lean.Server.RequestError
          { code := Lean.JsonRpc.ErrorCode.methodNotFound,
            message := toString "No RPC method '" ++ toString p.method ++ toString "' found" }
      Lean.Server.RequestM.bindWaitFindSnap doc
          (fun s =>
            decide (s.endPos ≥ callPos) ||
              (Lean.Server.userRpcProcedures.find? s.env p.method).isSome)
          throwNotFound fun snap =>
          match Lean.Server.userRpcProcedures.find? snap.env p.method with
          | some procName =>
            have options := snap.cmdState.scopes.head!.opts;
            match Lean.Server.evalRpcProcedure✝ snap.env options procName with
            | Except.ok x => x.wrapper p.sessionId p.params
            | Except.error e =>
              throwThe Lean.Server.RequestError
                { code := Lean.JsonRpc.ErrorCode.internalError,
                  message :=
                    toString "Failed to evaluate RPC constant '" ++ toString procName ++
                        toString "': " ++
                      toString e }

doc:
Keeps track of panel widget instances that should be displayed.

Instances can be registered for display global
(i.e., persisted in `.olean`s) and locally (not persisted)

For globally displayed widgets
we cannot store a `WidgetInstance` in the persistent state
because it contains a `StateM` closure.
Instead, we add a global constant of type `WidgetInstance`
to the environment, and store its name in the extension.

For locally displayed ones, we just store a `WidgetInstance`
in the extension directly.
This is okay because it is never persisted.

The (persistent) entries are then of the form `(h, n)`
where `h` is a hash stored in the `moduleRegistry`
and `n` is the name of a `WidgetInstance` global constant.

The extension state maps each `h` as above
to a list of entries that can be either global or local ones.
Each element of the state indicates that the widget module `h`
should be displayed with the given `WidgetInstance` as its arguments.

This is similar to a parametric attribute, except that:
- parametric attributes map at most one parameter to one tagged declaration,
  whereas we may display multiple instances of a single widget module; and
- parametric attributes use the same type for local and global entries,
  which we cannot do owing to the closure.

value.text:
fun pos => do
  let doc ← Lean.Server.RequestM.readDoc
  have filemap : Lean.FileMap := doc.meta.text
  Lean.Server.RequestM.mapTaskCostly
      (Lean.Server.RequestM.findInfoTreeAtPos doc (filemap.lspPosToUtf8Pos pos) true) fun x =>
      match x with
      |
      some infoTree@h:(Lean.Elab.InfoTree.context (Lean.Elab.PartialContextInfo.commandCtx cc) t) =>
        liftM
          ({ toCommandContextInfo := cc }.runMetaM { } do
            let env ← Lean.getEnv
            let ws' ← Lean.Widget.evalPanelWidgets
            let ws' ←
              Array.mapM
                  (fun wi => do
                    let name? ←
                      Option.mapM
                          (fun x => do
                            let uwd ← Lean.Widget.evalUserWidgetDefinition wi.id
                            pure uwd.name)
                          (Option.filter
                            (fun x => x.type.isConstOf `Lean.Widget.UserWidgetDefinition)
                            (env.find? wi.id))
                    pure { toWidgetInstance := wi, name? := name? })
                  ws'
            have ws : List Lean.Elab.UserWidgetInfo :=
              Lean.Widget.widgetInfosAt? filemap infoTree pos.line
            let ws ←
              Array.mapM
                  (fun wi => do
                    let name? ←
                      Option.mapM
                          (fun x => do
                            let uwd ← Lean.Widget.evalUserWidgetDefinition wi.id
                            pure uwd.name)
                          (Option.filter
                            (fun x => x.type.isConstOf `Lean.Widget.UserWidgetDefinition)
                            (env.find? wi.id))
                    pure
                        { toWidgetInstance := wi.toWidgetInstance,
                          range? := Lean.Syntax.Range.toLspRange filemap <$> wi.stx.getRange?,
                          name? := name? })
                  ws.toArray
            pure { widgets := ws' ++ ws })
      | x => pure { widgets := ∅ }

doc:
Add a "try this" suggestion. This has two effects:

* A widget diagnostic is displayed, saying `Try this: <suggestion>` with a link on `<suggestion>`
  to apply the suggestion
* A code action is added, which will apply the suggestion.

The parameters are:
* `ref`: the span of the widget diagnostic
* `s`: a `Suggestion`, which contains
  * `suggestion`: the replacement text
  * `preInfo?`: an optional string shown immediately before the replacement text in the widget
    message (only)
  * `postInfo?`: an optional string shown immediately after the replacement text in the widget
    message (only)
  * `messageData?`: an optional `MessageData` displayed instead of `suggestion`.
    If set, implies `diffGranularity = .none`.
  * `toCodeActionTitle?`: an optional function `String → String` describing how to transform the
    pretty-printed suggestion text into the code action text which appears in the lightbulb menu.
    If `none`, we simply prepend `"Try This: "` to the suggestion text.
* `origSpan?`: a syntax object whose span is the actual text to be replaced by `suggestion`.
  If not provided it defaults to `ref`.
* `header`: a string that begins the display. By default, it is `"Try this:"`.
* `codeActionPrefix?`: an optional string to be used as the prefix of the replacement text if the
  suggestion does not have a custom `toCodeActionTitle?`. If not provided, `"Try this: "` is used.
* `diffGranularity`: How to compute the diff display in the suggestion. Defaults to only displaying
  the inserted string.

  (origSpan? : Option Lean.Syntax := none) (header : String := "Try this:")
  (codeActionPrefix? : Option String := none)
  (diffGranularity : Lean.Meta.Hint.DiffGranularity := Lean.Meta.Hint.DiffGranularity.none)
  (footer : Lean.MessageData := Lean.MessageData.nil) : Lean.CoreM Unit

  Lean.logInfoAt ref
      (Lean.toMessageData header ++ Lean.toMessageData suggs ++ Lean.toMessageData footer)

Returns the syntax for an `exact` or `refine` (as indicated by `useRefine`) tactic corresponding to
`e` as well as a `MessageData` representation with hover information.
If `exposeNames` is `true`, prepends the tactic with `expose_names.` Note that the tactic is
always generated within `withExposedNames` to avoid generating unprintable characters.

fun e useRefine =>
  Lean.withOptions (fun x => Lean.Option.set x Lean.pp.mvars false)
    (Lean.Meta.withExposedNames do
      let exprStx ← Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.delabToRefinableSyntax e
      have __do_jp : Lean.TSyntax `tactic → Lean.MetaM (Lean.TSyntax `tactic × Lean.MessageData) :=
        fun tac => do
        let exprMessage ← Lean.addMessageContext (Lean.MessageData.ofExpr e)
        have tacMessage : Lean.MessageData :=
          if useRefine = true then Lean.toMessageData "refine " ++ Lean.toMessageData exprMessage
          else Lean.toMessageData "exact " ++ Lean.toMessageData exprMessage
        pure (tac, tacMessage)
      if useRefine = true then do
          let tac ←
            do
              let info ← Lean.MonadRef.mkInfoFromRefPos
              let _ ← Lean.getCurrMacroScope
              let _ ← Lean.MonadQuotation.getContext
              pure
                  {
                    raw :=
                      Lean.Syntax.node2 info `Lean.Parser.Tactic.refine
                        (Lean.Syntax.atom info "refine") exprStx.raw }
          __do_jp tac
        else do
          let tac ←
            do
              let info ← Lean.MonadRef.mkInfoFromRefPos
              let _ ← Lean.getCurrMacroScope
              let _ ← Lean.MonadQuotation.getContext
              pure
                  {
                    raw :=
                      Lean.Syntax.node2 info `Lean.Parser.Tactic.exact
                        (Lean.Syntax.atom info "exact") exprStx.raw }
          __do_jp tac)

fun addSubgoalsMsg checkState? e =>
  Lean.withOptions (fun x => Lean.Option.set x Lean.pp.mvars false) do
    let mvars ← liftM (Lean.Meta.getMVars e)
    have hasMVars : Bool := !mvars.isEmpty
    let __x ← liftM (Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.mkExactSuggestionSyntax✝ e hasMVars)
    match __x with
      | (suggestion, messageData) =>
        match checkState? with
        | some checkState => do
          let __x ← Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.mkValidatedTactic✝ suggestion messageData checkState
          match __x with
            | some (suggestion, messageData) =>
              have __do_jp := fun postInfo? =>
                pure
                  (Sum.inl
                    { suggestion := Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.SuggestionText.tsyntax suggestion,
                      postInfo? := postInfo?, messageData? := some messageData });
              if (!addSubgoalsMsg || mvars.isEmpty) = true then do
                let postInfo? ← pure none
                __do_jp postInfo?
              else
                have str := "\n-- Remaining subgoals:";
                do
                let __s ←
                  forIn mvars str fun g __s =>
                      have str := __s;
                      do
                      let __do_lift ← liftM g.getType
                      let __do_lift ← Lean.instantiateMVars __do_lift
                      let e ←
                        liftM (Lean.Meta.withExposedNames (Lean.PrettyPrinter.ppExpr __do_lift))
                      have str : String := str ++ (Std.Format.text "\n-- ⊢ " ++ e).pretty
                      pure (ForInStep.yield str)
                have str : String := __s
                let postInfo? ← pure (some str)
                __do_jp postInfo?
            | x =>
              have messageData :=
                Lean.toMessageData "(expose_names; " ++ Lean.toMessageData messageData ++
                  Lean.toMessageData ")";
              pure
                (Sum.inr
                  (Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.mkFailedToMakeTacticMsg✝
                    (Lean.toMessageData "a " ++
                        Lean.toMessageData (if hasMVars = true then "partial " else "") ++
                      Lean.toMessageData "proof")
                    messageData))
        | x =>
          pure
            (Sum.inl { suggestion := Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.SuggestionText.tsyntax suggestion })

doc:
Add a list of "try this" suggestions as a single "try these" suggestion. This has two effects:

* A widget diagnostic is displayed, saying `Try these: <list of suggestions>` with a link on
  each suggestion in `<list of suggestions>` to apply each suggestion
* A code action for each suggestion is added, which will apply the suggestion.

The parameters are:
* `ref`: the span of the widget diagnostic
* `suggestions`: an array of `Suggestion`s, which each contain
  * `suggestion`: the replacement text
  * `preInfo?`: an optional string shown immediately before the replacement text in the widget
    message (only)
  * `postInfo?`: an optional string shown immediately after the replacement text in the widget
    message (only)
  * `messageData?`: an optional `MessageData` displayed instead of `suggestion`.
    If set, implies `diffGranularity = .none`.
  * `toCodeActionTitle?`: an optional function `String → String` describing how to transform the
    pretty-printed suggestion text into the code action text which appears in the lightbulb menu.
    If `none`, we simply prepend `"Try this: "` to the suggestion text.
* `origSpan?`: a syntax object whose span is the actual text to be replaced by `suggestion`.
  If not provided it defaults to `ref`.
* `header`: a string that precedes the list. By default, it is `"Try these:"`.
* `style?` (**deprecated**): unused.
* `codeActionPrefix?`: an optional string to be used as the prefix of the replacement text for all
  suggestions which do not have a custom `toCodeActionTitle?`. If not provided, `"Try this: "` is
  used.
* `diffGranularity`: How to compute the diff display in the suggestion. Defaults to only displaying
  the inserted string.

def Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.addSuggestions (ref : Lean.Syntax)
  (suggestions : Array Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.Suggestion) (origSpan? : Option Lean.Syntax := none)
  (header : String := "Try these:")
  (style? : Option Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.SuggestionStyle := none)
  (codeActionPrefix? : Option String := none)
  (diffGranularity : Lean.Meta.Hint.DiffGranularity := Lean.Meta.Hint.DiffGranularity.none)
  (footer : Lean.MessageData := Lean.MessageData.nil) : Lean.CoreM Unit

value.text:
fun ref suggestions origSpan? header style? codeActionPrefix? diffGranularity footer =>
  have __do_jp := fun __r =>
    have hintSuggestions :=
      Array.map
        (fun s =>
          { toTryThisSuggestion := s, span? := origSpan?, diffGranularity := diffGranularity })
        suggestions;
    do
    let suggs ← Lean.Meta.Hint.mkSuggestionsMessage hintSuggestions ref codeActionPrefix? true
    Lean.logInfoAt ref
        (Lean.toMessageData header ++ Lean.toMessageData suggs ++ Lean.toMessageData footer);
  if suggestions.isEmpty = true then do
    let __r ← Lean.throwErrorAt ref (Lean.toMessageData "No suggestions available")
    __do_jp __r
  else __do_jp ()

doc:
Returns a possibly modified version of `tac` that succeeds in `initialState`, prepending
`expose_names` if necessary. If `expectedType?` is non-`none`, the tactic is only considered to have
"succeeded" if the resulting goal is equal (up to `Expr` equality modulo metavariable instantiation)
to the provided type. Returns `none` if the tactic fails even with `expose_names`.

Remark: We cannot determine if a tactic requires `expose_names` merely by inspecting its syntax
(shadowed variables are delaborated without daggers) nor the underlying `Expr` used to produce it
(some inaccessible names may be implicit arguments that do not appear in the delaborated syntax).

value.text:
fun tac msg initialState expectedType? => do
  let e ←
    tryCatch
        (do
          Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.evalTacticWithState✝ initialState tac expectedType?
          EarlyReturnT.return (some (tac, msg)))
        fun x => do
        let tac ←
          do
            let info ← Lean.MonadRef.mkInfoFromRefPos
            let _ ← Lean.getCurrMacroScope
            let _ ← Lean.MonadQuotation.getContext
            pure
                {
                  raw :=
                    Lean.Syntax.node3 info `Lean.Parser.Tactic.paren (Lean.Syntax.atom info "(")
                      (Lean.Syntax.node1 info `Lean.Parser.Tactic.tacticSeq
                        (Lean.Syntax.node1 info `Lean.Parser.Tactic.tacticSeq1Indented
                          (Lean.Syntax.node3 info `null
                            (Lean.Syntax.node1 info `Lean.Parser.Tactic.exposeNames
                              (Lean.Syntax.atom info "expose_names"))
                            (Lean.Syntax.atom info ";") tac.raw)))
                      (Lean.Syntax.atom info ")") }
        let e ←
          tryCatch
              (do
                Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.evalTacticWithState✝ initialState tac expectedType?
                EarlyReturnT.return
                    (some
                      (tac,
                        Lean.toMessageData "(expose_names; " ++ Lean.toMessageData msg ++
                          Lean.toMessageData ")")))
              fun x => EarlyReturnT.return none
        EarlyReturn.runK e (fun r => EarlyReturnT.return r) fun r => ExceptT.run (pure r)
  EarlyReturn.runK e (fun r => pure r) fun r => pure r

This is a code action provider that looks for `TryThisInfo` nodes and supplies a code action to
apply the replacement.

value.text:
fun params snap => do
  let doc ← Lean.Server.RequestM.readDoc
  pure
      (Lean.Elab.InfoTree.foldInfo
        (fun _ctx info result =>
          (match info with
            | Lean.Elab.Info.ofCustomInfo { stx := stx, value := value } =>
              match Dynamic.get? Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.TryThisInfo value with
              |
              some { edit := edit, codeActionTitle := codeActionTitle, suggestion := suggestion } =>
                match stx.getRange? with
                | some stxRange =>
                  have stxRange := doc.meta.text.utf8RangeToLspRange stxRange;
                  if stxRange.start.line ≤ params.range.end.line then
                    if params.range.start.line ≤ stxRange.end.line then
                      result.push
                        {
                          eager :=
                            { title := codeActionTitle, kind? := some "quickfix",
                              edit? :=
                                some
                                  (Lean.Lsp.WorkspaceEdit.ofTextEdit doc.versionedIdentifier
                                    edit) } }
                    else pure result
                  else pure result
                | x => result
              | x => result
            | x => result).run)
        #[] snap.infoTree)

doc:
Add `exact e` or `refine e` suggestions if they can be successfully generated; for those that
cannot, display messages indicating the invalid generated tactics.

The parameters are:
* `ref`: the span of the widget diagnostic
* `es`: the array of replacement expressions
* `origSpan?`: a syntax object whose span is the actual text to be replaced by `suggestion`.
  If not provided it defaults to `ref`.
* `addSubgoalsMsg`: if true (default false), any remaining subgoals will be shown after
  `Remaining subgoals:`
* `codeActionPrefix?`: an optional string to be used as the prefix of the replacement text for all
  suggestions which do not have a custom `toCodeActionTitle?`. If not provided, `"Try this: "` is
  used.
* `checkState?`: if passed, the tactic state in which the generated tactics will be validated,
  inserting `expose_names` if necessary.
* `tacticErrorAsInfo`: if true (default true), invalid generated tactics will log info messages
  instead of throwing an error. The default behavior differs from `addExactSuggestion` because
  throwing an error means that any subsequent suggestions will not be displayed. Has no effect if
  `checkState?` is `none`.

  (origSpan? : Option Lean.Syntax := none) (addSubgoalsMsg : Bool := false)
  (codeActionPrefix? : Option String := none)

  Lean.Elab.Tactic.TacticM Unit

fun ref es origSpan? addSubgoalsMsg codeActionPrefix? checkState? tacticErrorAsInfo => do
  let suggestionOrMessages ←
    Array.mapM (Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.addExactSuggestionCore✝ addSubgoalsMsg checkState?) es
  have suggestions : Array Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.Suggestion := #[]
  have messages : Array Lean.MessageData := #[]
  let __s ←
    forIn suggestionOrMessages (suggestions, messages) fun suggestionOrMessage __s =>
        have suggestions := __s.1;
        have messages := __s.2;
        match suggestionOrMessage with
        | Sum.inl suggestion =>
          have suggestions := suggestions.push suggestion;
          pure (ForInStep.yield (suggestions, messages))
        | Sum.inr message =>
          have __do_jp := fun __r =>
            have messages := messages.push message;
            pure (ForInStep.yield (suggestions, messages));
          if tacticErrorAsInfo = true then __do_jp ()
          else do
            let __r ← Lean.throwError message
            __do_jp __r
  have suggestions : Array Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.Suggestion := __s.1
  have messages : Array Lean.MessageData := __s.2
  liftM
      (Lean.Meta.Tactic.TryThis.addSuggestions ref suggestions origSpan? "Try these:" none
        codeActionPrefix?)
  forIn messages PUnit.unit fun message __s => do
      Lean.logInfo message
      pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
  pure ()

Add an `exact e` or `refine e` suggestion.

The parameters are:
* `ref`: the span of the widget diagnostic
* `e`: the replacement expression
* `origSpan?`: a syntax object whose span is the actual text to be replaced by `suggestion`.
  If not provided it defaults to `ref`.
* `addSubgoalsMsg`: if true (default false), any remaining subgoals will be shown after
  `Remaining subgoals:`
* `codeActionPrefix?`: an optional string to be used as the prefix of the replacement text if the
  suggestion does not have a custom `toCodeActionTitle?`. If not provided, `"Try this: "` is used.
* `checkState?`: if passed, the tactic state in which the generated tactic will be validated,
  inserting `expose_names` if necessary.
* `tacticErrorAsInfo`: if true (default false), if a generated tactic is invalid (e.g., due to a
   pretty-printing issue), the resulting error message will be logged as an info message instead of
   being thrown as an error. Has no effect if `checkState?` is `none`.

Evaluates `tac` in `initialState` without recovery or sorrying on elaboration failure. If
`expectedType?` is non-`none`, an error is thrown if the resulting goal type is not equal to the
provided type (up to `Expr` equality modulo metavariable instantiation).

fun initialState tac expectedType? => do
  let currState ← Lean.saveState
  initialState.restore
  tryFinally
      (do
        Lean.Elab.Term.withoutErrToSorry
            (Lean.Elab.Tactic.withoutRecover (Lean.Elab.Tactic.evalTactic tac.raw))
        match expectedType? with
          | some expectedType => do
            let __do_lift ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.getMainGoal
            let type ← liftM __do_lift.getType
            let type ← Lean.instantiateMVars type
            let expectedType ← Lean.instantiateMVars expectedType
            if (type != expectedType) = true then
                Lean.throwError (Lean.toMessageData "Tactic did not produce expected goal")
              else pure ()
          | x => pure ())
      currState.restore

The tactics `refine`, `apply` and `refine'` are similar, but they handle metavariables slightly

doc:
Given two iterators `left` and `right`, `left.zip right` is an iterator that yields pairs of
outputs of `left` and `right`. When one of them terminates,
the `zip` iterator will also terminate.

**Marble diagram:**

```text
left               --a        ---b        --c
right                 --x         --y        --⊥
left.zip right     -----(a, x)------(b, y)-----⊥
```

**Termination properties:**

* `Finite` instance: only if either `left` or `right` is finite and the other is productive
* `Productive` instance: only if `left` and `right` are productive

There are situations where `left.zip right` is finite (or productive) but none of the instances
above applies. For example, if the computation happens in an `Except` monad and `left` immediately
fails when calling `step`, then `left.zip right` will also do so. In such a case, the `Finite`
(or `Productive`) instance needs to be proved manually.

**Performance:**

This combinator incurs an additional O(1) cost with each step taken by `left` or `right`.

Right now, the compiler does not unbox the internal state, leading to worse performance than
possible.

doc:
Builds a proof of `String.ofList l₁ ≠ String.ofList l₂` for two distinct string literals.

The proof avoids both `String.decEq` (expensive UTF-8 byte array comparison) and full
`List Char` comparison. It reduces to `List Char` via `String.ofList_injective`, then
proves the lists differ using one of two strategies depending on whether the strings
share a common prefix of the shorter string's full length:

- **Different characters at position `i`**: Uses
  `congrArg (fun l => (List.get!Internal l i).toNat)` to project down to `Nat`, then
  `Nat.ne_of_beq_eq_false rfl` for a single `Nat.beq` comparison. This avoids `Decidable`
  instances entirely — the kernel only evaluates `Nat.beq` on two concrete natural numbers.

- **One string is a prefix of the other**: Uses `congrArg (List.drop n ·)` where `n` is the
  shorter string's length, then `List.cons_ne_nil` to prove the non-empty tail differs from `[]`.
  This avoids `decide` entirely since `cons_ne_nil` is a definitional proof.

Try to close main goal using `x target tag`, where `target` is the type of the main goal and `tag` is its user name.

If `checkNewUnassigned` is true, then throws an error if the resulting value has metavariables that were created during the execution of `x`.
If it is false, then it is the responsibility of `x` to add such metavariables to the goal list.

During the execution of `x`:
* The local context is that of the main goal.
* The goal list has the main goal removed.
* It is allowable to modify the goal list, for example with `Lean.Elab.Tactic.pushGoals`.

On failure, the main goal remains at the front of the goal list.

                        Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentExpr val) ++

doc: Apply the tactic everywhere.

Runs the given `atLocal` and `atTarget` methods on each of the locations selected by the given `loc`.
* If `loc` is a list of locations, runs at each specified hypothesis (and finally the goal if `⊢` is included),
  and fails if any of the tactic applications fail.
* If `loc` is `*`, runs at the target first and then the hypotheses in reverse order.
  If `atTarget` closes the main goal, `withLocation` does not run `atLocal`.
  If all tactic applications fail, `withLocation` with call `failed` with the main goal mvar.

value.text:
fun loc atLocal atTarget failed =>
  match loc with
  | Lean.Elab.Tactic.Location.targets hyps type => do
    Array.forM
        (fun hyp =>
          Lean.Elab.Tactic.withMainContext do
            let fvarId ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.getFVarId hyp
            atLocal fvarId)
        hyps
    if type = true then Lean.Elab.Tactic.withMainContext atTarget else pure ()
  | Lean.Elab.Tactic.Location.wildcard => do
    let worked ←
      Lean.Elab.Tactic.tryTactic
          (Lean.Elab.withSaveInfoContext (Lean.Elab.Tactic.withMainContext atTarget))
    let e ←
      tryCatch
          (do
            let g ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.getMainGoal
            ExceptT.run (pure g))
          fun x => EarlyReturnT.return ()
    EarlyReturn.runK e (fun r => pure r) fun g =>
        g.withContext
          (have worked := worked;
          do
          let __do_lift ← Lean.getLCtx
          let __s ←
            forIn __do_lift.getFVarIds.reverse worked fun fvarId __s =>
                have worked := __s;
                do
                let __do_lift ← liftM fvarId.getDecl
                if __do_lift.isImplementationDetail = true then pure (ForInStep.yield worked)
                  else do
                    let __do_lift ←
                      Lean.Elab.Tactic.tryTactic
                          (Lean.Elab.withSaveInfoContext
                            (Lean.Elab.Tactic.withMainContext (atLocal fvarId)))
                    have worked : Bool := worked || __do_lift
                    pure (ForInStep.yield worked)
          have worked : Bool := __s
          if worked = true then pure ()
            else do
              let __do_lift ← Lean.Elab.Tactic.getMainGoal
              failed __do_lift)

implementing them would ensure a `cls type` instance. If there are no conditional
instances to support this, returns `#[type]`. If there's already a `cls type` instance,
returns `#[]`.

doc:
Helper for deriving instances along with all dependencies.
Given a one-parameter class `className` and a type `type`,
uses pre-existing conditional instances to figure out which types would
suffice to be implemented, then runs `mkCmd` on each type with fresh macro scopes.

The commands are generated and elaborated one at a time.

fun className type extraDeps mkCmd => do
  let types ←
    Lean.Elab.Command.liftTermElabM (Lean.Elab.ConfigEval.planDerivation✝ className type extraDeps)
  let env ← Lean.getEnv
  forIn types PUnit.unit fun type' __s => do
      let cmd ←
        Lean.Elab.Command.liftTermElabM
            (tryCatch (Lean.withFreshMacroScope (mkCmd type')) fun ex =>
              have cls := `Elab.ConfigEval;
              do
              let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
              have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.Elab.TermElabM Lean.Command := fun __r => do
                Lean.setEnv env
                throw ex
              if __do_lift = true then do
                  let __r ←
                    Lean.addTrace cls
                        (Lean.toMessageData "failure deriving instance for `" ++
                              Lean.toMessageData type' ++
                            Lean.toMessageData "`: " ++
                          Lean.toMessageData ex.toMessageData)
                  __do_jp __r
                else __do_jp ())
      Lean.Elab.Command.elabCommand cmd.raw
      have cls : Lean.Name := `Elab.ConfigEval
      let __do_lift ← Lean.isTracingEnabledFor cls
      if __do_lift = true then do
          Lean.addTrace cls
              (Lean.toMessageData "added instance of " ++
                      Lean.toMessageData (Lean.MessageData.ofConstName className) ++
                    Lean.toMessageData " for  `" ++
                  Lean.toMessageData type' ++
                Lean.toMessageData "`")
          pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
        else pure (ForInStep.yield PUnit.unit)
  pure ()

doc:
Interprets `cfg` as configuration item or list of configuration items.

Items are interpreted in a way that allows user-defined configurations.
Nearly anything that looks like configuration items or lists of configuration items
will be interpreted. We're expecting an item that has one of the following formats:
- `"(" ident/atom ":=" syntax ")"`
- `"+" ident/atom`
- `"-" ident/atom`

The specification:
- A null node is a list of configurations
- A one-argument node is considered to be a wrapper like `optConfig` or `configItem`.
- A node with at two arguments starting with a "+"/"-" atom and whose second
  argument is an ident or atom is a `posConfigItem`/`negConfigItem`
- A node with at most five arguments starting with a "(" atom and whose second argument
  is an ident or atom is a `valConfigItem`. The fourth argument is the value,
  and it is allowed to have arbitary syntax (it does not need to be a `Term`).
- A bare atom is considered to be a `"+"` option.

We trust that any atoms are valid as idents. The atom will be parsed using `String.toName`
to form the name. (Small optimization: if the name doesn't contain `.`, we use `Name.mkSimple`
to skip parsing. Atoms must not contain numerals or `«»` escapes.)

On interpretation error, `onErr` is called with the current configuration object and the offending
syntax item. It may process the item itself or otherwise throw an error. We leave it to `onErr`
to decide what to do for items containing `Syntax.missing`.

    do
    let e ← Lean.Elab.Term.withSynthesize (Lean.Elab.Term.elabTermEnsuringType stx.raw ty?)
    let e ← Lean.instantiateMVars e
    have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.Elab.TermElabM α := fun __r => do
      let __do_lift ← liftM (Lean.Meta.getMVars e)
      let __do_lift ← Lean.Elab.Term.logUnassignedUsingErrorInfos __do_lift
      have __do_jp : Unit → Lean.Elab.TermElabM α := fun __r =>
        Lean.catchInternalId Lean.Elab.unsupportedSyntaxExceptionId

          have extra :=

            | x => Lean.toMessageData "";

          let __r ← Lean.Elab.throwAbortTerm

    if e.hasSorry = true then

          let __r ←

                  Lean.toMessageData (Lean.indentExpr e))
